turns.user: Explain why a load balancer sends requests to several servers.
turns.assistant:
**Answer**

A load balancer spreads incoming work across several servers so one machine does not get overloaded.

**Why**

When many people use an app at once, a single server can slow down or crash. A load balancer sits in front of those servers and routes each request to one of them.

That spreads the work. Each server handles part of the traffic, so the app stays fast and stays up if one server fails.

**Example**

Imagine a busy restaurant with one cashier. Lines grow long. Add more cashiers and a host who sends each customer to the next free cashier. The host is the load balancer; the cashiers are the servers.
